claim_as_shown: Winning a new customer costs five to 25 times more than keeping an existing one, depending on the industry.
title: The Value of Keeping the Right Customers (Amy Gallo)
notes: Exact source line: 'Depending on which study you believe, and what industry you're in, acquiring a new customer is anywhere from five to 25 times more expensive than retaining an existing one.' Global figure; no Indian equivalent found. Slide must say the ratio varies by industry. claim_as_shown: Keeping 5% more of your customers can lift profits by 25% to 95%.
publisher: Harvard Business Review, citing research by Frederick Reichheld of Bain and Company
title: The Value of Keeping the Right Customers (Amy Gallo)
notes: Exact source line: 'research done by Frederick Reichheld of Bain and Company (the inventor of the net promoter score) shows increasing customer retention rates by 5% increases profits by 25% to 95%.' Corroborated on Bain's own site: 'Retaining customers is the real challenge' (Bain and Company, 2006, https://www.bain.com/insights/retaining-customers-is-the-real-challenge/): 'by increasing retention by as little as 5 per cent, profits can be boosted by as much as 95 per cent.' The Bain page opens in a browser but returns 403 to curl (Cloudflare), so cite HBR on the slide. Global figure.

claim_as_shown: The southwest monsoon normally reaches Kerala around 1 June and has left the whole country around 15 October.
publisher: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
title: Monsoon Information: Onset (web page) and Frequently Asked Questions on Monsoon (PDF)
notes: Exact source lines. Onset page: 'Southwest monsoon normally sets in over Kerala around 1st June. It advances northwards, usually in surges, and covers the entire country around 15th July.' Withdrawal, IMD FAQ PDF (https://mausam.imd.gov.in/imd_latest/monsoonfaq.pdf, Q35): 'SW monsoon is withdrawn from the southern peninsula and hence from the entire country around 15th October'. Use for the 12-month reminder calendar (pre-monsoon checks in April and May, post-monsoon tank cleaning in October and November). The page shows no publication year; IMD's site lists Monsoon Report 2025 alongside, so year recorded as 2025 (current IMD web content). Screenshot: assets/img/s05/imd-monsoon-onset.png.
